definition: Judicious means having or showing careful, sound judgment.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word judicious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know judicious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A judicious pause before answering has spared the ambassador more headlines than any speech.
A sensible choice avoids the obvious mistakes; a judicious one has weighed even the interests that weren't in the room.
Sagacious goes past judicious — beyond one well-weighed decision to a lifetime's proven depth of judgment.

Prudent is careful to steer around future harm — the prudent driver slows before the icy bridge. Judicious is wider: it weighs every side of a decision, benefits as well as risks, the near term against the far. A choice can be prudent without being judicious if caution was its only virtue.

Levelheaded describes temperament — staying calm and clear while others panic, so nothing rash gets decided. Judicious describes the judgment itself: every interest weighed, the long term set beside the short. A levelheaded person keeps their footing in the storm; a judicious one also picks the right road afterward.

Judicious means having or showing careful, sound judgment.
Offered triple money to clear-cut the old-growth stand, the timber cooperative's manager chose a more judicious course.
She sold the storm-downed trunks first, thinned the crowded east slope where the foresters wanted light, and left the seed trees alone.
The mill got most of its order; the hillside kept its future; and the members who had shouted "take the money" were quietly glad, ten years on, that she hadn't.
Judicious is the exact word because the manager shows careful, sound judgment — every interest weighed, the near term set against the long, nothing decided in heat.
The word doesn't mean timid or slow; it means the thinking was done properly before the acting.
Judges gave the word its name, and it still carries their obligation: decide as if the future will read the decision.
Judicious is for decisions in which the weighing shows — every interest heard, the long term set beside the short.
This unit's canny also judges well, but for its own side of the table; myopic names the failure judicious avoids, judgment that can't see past this quarter.
Prudent guards against harm; judicious balances the whole ledger.

The flood money arrived with one instruction: spend it where it does the most good.
Mayor Ito discovered how many ways a town can read that sentence.
The hardware store wanted the bridge first; the school board wanted the gym dried out before mold set in; the farmers, quietest of all, needed the drainage ditches dug before spring.

Ito spent two weeks walking the town with a notebook and gave a judicious answer: ditches first, because a second flood would take the bridge and the gym with it; then the gym; the bridge repair phased over two summers.
The council noted that even the road crews — who had spoken at no meeting — found their culverts on the list.
When the vote came, it carried without a single speech against it.
